html:
An Indian steel company founded on 26 August 1907 as the Tata Iron and Steel Company. It built Asia's first privately owned integrated steel works, at Sakchi in eastern India, around which grew the town of Jamshedpur.

The plan was the life's dream of Jamsetji Tata, founder of the Tata Group, who died in 1904 before it was realised. His sons carried it out. British investors were not interested, so they raised the money from thousands of Indian investors, a point of pride in the years of the Swadeshi movement for Indian-made goods. Geologists found iron ore and coal close together in the area, and the first steel was made in 1912.

The works supplied rails and shell steel to Britain in the First of the world wars. Jamshedpur was planned as a company town with housing, hospitals and parks, and Tata became known for an early eight-hour day and welfare schemes. After independence it remained private while the state built its own steel plants. In 2007 it bought the Anglo-Dutch steelmaker Corus, then one of the largest foreign takeovers by an Indian company.
